<p>Is the author really <em>Anonymous </em>or is that a quote from the Tennessee sideline chain team/line judge who tried to Jedi mind trick the SEC officials Saturday into thinking the down count for the vols was third down instead of fourth down? We realize Tennessee’s education system is weak but counting 1 2 3 4 is not too much to require of SEC officials. It is perfectly reasonable to expect the counting of the game downs to be perfectly managed (or counting 11 vs. 12 vol defensive men on the field for that matter). Yes, we have plenty of reasons to be sore losers and suggest the officials should get the Tennessee game ball and all that, but instead, because we are Alabama fans, let’s be class acts, hold our nose and be gracious about Tennessee’s win. </p><p>Here goes…</p><p><em>Hey vols, congrats. You probably deserve to beat Alabama once every 15 years. I would not be surprised if we see you again in the SEC championship. Watch out now…Coach Saban is outstanding in rematches against opponents who beat him. So, enjoy your win today, vols. You are still tooth-limited hillbillies.</em></p><p>Doesn’t it feel good to take the high road even after a loss?!</p><p>Moving on some…do you feel the team spirit in the air?!&nbsp;It’s homecoming at the Capstone! I know many of you shared my disappointment in my unsuccessful run at HC queen last year, and the year before and…well, you get the picture.</p><p>However, the exploratory committee I commissioned has produced findings that my platform for a 2022 HC queen campaign is <em>sure</em> to succeed. This issue has been a problem in Tennessee for years but today has grown into a full-fledged worldwide crisis. So, this platform is for all the parents out there…<em>Cut Out the Mullet!</em> </p><p>You all have seen it…a person with short “business up front” hair from the frontal view and “party in the back” locks flowing down his back. The mullet movement is rabid amongst youngsters these days. How did this happen? According to <em>GQ Magazine</em>, the mullet began to resurge during the pandemic with more and more people binge watching <em>Tiger King</em> and not having access to barbers/hair salons. It grew into a style for “outsiders, rebels and anyone who wanted to stand out.” The article goes on to read, “The mullet requires zest and confidence.” </p><p>What happened to confidence coming from the belief the sun will come up tomorrow (it will Alabama fans) or from being prepared for a test or meeting (Alabama’s D may need to try growing their hair out some to “stand out” and regain that “confidence”).</p><p>Is this HC queen platform really more urgent than my past HC Queen platform of <em>Done with the Man Bun</em>, you ask? I believe it is, because the mullet is not being spotted on just a few folks here and there. It’s a widespread trend that could easily sneak up and engulf us. Ever think about what happens if your hair care professional comes down with the flu keeping her/him away from work and missing your scheduled appointment?! It could happen. Then pretty soon you feel more “confident” with the attention your mullet has gained, and, slowly, you embrace and double down on the look and even start entering mullet contests.
